title: Flight cancellations: Lufthansa strike and Italian air traffic control walkout hit Luxembourg flights - RTL Today
body: Flight cancellations: Lufthansa strike and Italian air traffic control walkout hit Luxembourg flights - RTL Today Home Play Radio RTL Lëtzebuerg RTL Infos Home Play Radio News Luxembourg World Fact Check Business & Tech Think Lab Science & Environment Flight cancellations Lufthansa strike and Italian air traffic control walkout hit Luxembourg flights RTL Lëtzebuerg adapted for RTL Today Flights to and from Munich, Frankfurt, Milan, and Pescara are among those cancelled, with Luxembourg air passengers facing a disrupted Friday. Published: 10.04.26 14:22 © AFP Luxembourg travellers are facing major disruptions on Friday as two separate strike actions combine to wreak havoc on the flight schedule at Findel Airport. Lufthansa cabin crew have walked out until 10pm on Friday evening, after collective bargaining negotiations over improved working conditions failed to make progress. Hundreds of flights have already been cancelled across Germany, with departures and arrivals at Frankfurt and Munich most heavily affected, alongside Cologne-Bonn, Düsseldorf, and Berlin. Around 20,000 cabin crew members work for Lufthansa. Luxembourg flights impacted Several routes to and from Luxembourg have been cancelled as a result. The Friday morning flight to Frankfurt, scheduled for 8.20am, did not operate, nor did the 9:40am and nor will the 4.45pm services to Munich. Inbound flights have been equally affected, with the 9.05am arrival from Munich failing to land in Luxembourg, and the 4.10pm service also cancelled. The industrial action in Italy has added further complications. A strike by Italian air traffic controllers has resulted in the cancellation of the 12.20pm flight to Pescara and the 2.40pm service to Milan-Linate.
